description: Global StackVo settings living in <root>/.env — contract v1. Flat KEY=VALUE, no quoting, no interpolation, no multi-line values (the loader splits naively on the first '='). Every key below is typed, defaulted, and tagged with the files that read it, measured rather than asserted: `tools/measure-env-usage.mjs` scans this repository and `tests/env-consumers.spec.js` fails when the lists stop matching.

source.note: There is no `.env.example`. This said `.env.example`, 159 keys, and both halves were fossils: the file went with the Bash implementation, and 159 was that file's count rather than this document's. The defaults live in `src-tauri/src/config.rs` (`SETTINGS` and `LEGACY_SERVICES`, merged into `EMBEDDED`), and `.env` is written only when a setting is changed — so a workspace with no `.env` at all is the normal state, not an unconfigured one. `keys` is what this document describes, checked by `tests/env-consumers.spec.js`.

rules: Lines starting with '#' and blank lines are ignored.
Split on the FIRST '='; everything after it is the value, verbatim, trimmed.
Values are NEVER quoted. A quoted value keeps its quotes and will be wrong.
'true'/'false' are the only accepted booleans (lowercase). Anything else is falsy.
List values are comma-separated with no spaces after the comma.
parsing.note: docker compose --env-file consumes the same file, so keys must also be valid Compose interpolation names: ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$.

statusLegend.active: Read by at least one component today.
statusLegend.dead: Present in .env.example but nothing in the checkout reads it. Measured by tools/measure-env-usage.mjs, not by hand — the hand-run version of this was wrong for 12 keys.
statusLegend.conflicting: Active, but overlaps or contradicts another key — see CONFLICTS.md.

DEFAULT_TLD_SUFFIX.description: The TLD every service router and admin-UI template builds its hostname from (traefik.stackvo.loc, adminer.stackvo.loc…). Project domains are built from it too — the wizard writes <name>.<suffix> and adoption does the same, so changing this changes where new projects answer. Existing stackvo.json files keep the domain written in them, which is why changing this moves the tool URLs and every project made after it, but no project made before.

SSL_ENABLE.description: Emit TLS routers and self-signed certs.

LETSENCRYPT_ENABLE.description: No ACME resolver is generated. Meaningless for .loc domains.

IDLE_SUSPEND_MINUTES.description: Stop a project that Traefik has not routed anything to for this many minutes. 0 is off, which is the default: a project that stops behind somebody's back and then answers 502 is worse than one that stays up, so this is asked for rather than assumed. A project the access log has never mentioned is never suspended.

serverLimits._note: The web-server directives the Settings pane exposes. They were set by the app and described nowhere, which made the contract's single-source-of-truth claim untrue for exactly these ten keys — and it was the reason generator.rs and ServerLimitsPane.vue each carried their own copy of the defaults. nginx reads all ten; Caddy reads the two it has an equivalent for; Apache, Swoole and FrankenPHP read none. A value equal to the default emits no directive at all, so the defaults here are load-bearing rather than documentation.

SERVER_MAX_BODY_SIZE.description: Largest request body nginx accepts, and one of the two settings here Caddy also honours (`request_body max_size`). Rendered as `client_max_body_size` in the server block.

SERVER_CLIENT_BODY_TIMEOUT.description: Seconds to wait between reads of a request body. Rendered as `client_body_timeout` in the server block.

SERVER_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT.description: Seconds an idle keep-alive connection is held open. Rendered as `keepalive_timeout` in the server block.

SERVER_TCP_NODELAY.description: Send small packets immediately rather than coalescing them. Rendered as `tcp_nodelay` in the server block.

SERVER_GZIP.description: Compress responses. The other setting Caddy honours (`encode gzip`). Rendered as `gzip` in the server block.

SERVER_GZIP_COMP_LEVEL.description: Compression level, 1 to 9. Rendered as `gzip_comp_level` in the server block.

SERVER_GZIP_TYPES.description: Extra MIME types to compress. Empty means nginx's own list. Rendered as `gzip_types` in the server block.

SERVER_FASTCGI_CONNECT_TIMEOUT.description: Seconds to wait for the connection to PHP-FPM. Rendered as `fastcgi_connect_timeout` in the PHP location block.

SERVER_FASTCGI_SEND_TIMEOUT.description: Seconds to wait while sending the request to PHP. Rendered as `fastcgi_send_timeout` in the PHP location block.

SERVER_FASTCGI_TIMEOUT.description: Seconds to wait for PHP to answer. Kept under this name, without READ in it, because renaming it would move somebody's setting silently. Rendered as `fastcgi_read_timeout` in the PHP location block.

DEFAULT_PHP_VERSION.description: Older spelling of SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_PHP_DEFAULT. Copied forward when a .env carries it and not the current name, so a foreign checkout keeps working. Not shipped: it is a compatibility read, not a setting of ours.

DEFAULT_SERVER.description: Older spelling of SUPPORTED_SERVERS_DEFAULT. Copied forward when a .env carries it and not the current name, so a foreign checkout keeps working. Not shipped: it is a compatibility read, not a setting of ours.

DEFAULT_WEB_SERVER.description: Third spelling of the same idea (DEFAULT_SERVER, SUPPORTED_SERVERS_DEFAULT). No consumers.

DEFAULT_CACHE_SERVER.description: Value is also nonsensical (mysql is not a cache). Delete.

STACKVO_UI_ENABLE.description: The containerised web UI this desktop app replaced. Removed: the app no longer emits the service and the skeleton ships no core/ui, so the flag had nothing left to switch on.

SYSTEM_COMMAND_TIMEOUT.description: Never applied. Real build timeouts are hardcoded (nginx proxy_read_timeout 600s).

CACHE_TTL.description: Belonged to the retired web UI's Node cache, which went with it. Nothing in the desktop app has an equivalent.

LOG_LEVEL.note: Bash uses uppercase, pino expects lowercase. Readers MUST lowercase before handing to pino.
LOG_LEVEL.description: Nothing ever read it — not the generator, not a template. It survived an earlier sweep by sitting inside SERVICE_BLACKFIRE_LOG_LEVEL as a substring.

TRAEFIK_URL.description: Dashboard subdomain, never wired up. Traefik's api.dashboard=true is set unconditionally in compose/base.yml.

DOCKER_DEFAULT_NETWORK.description: External network; must be created before `up`.

DOCKER_FORCE_RECREATE.description: Dead. `up` passes --force-recreate unconditionally in some paths and never reads this.

DOCKER_REMOVE_ORPHANS.description: Dead. --remove-orphans is hardcoded in the `up` command.

HOST_UID.description: Derived at render time from getuid()/getgid(). Not shipped and not a setting: it is a fact about the machine the app is running on, and a written-down value would pin one developer's ids into everybody's generated files.
HOST_UID.v1Change: OBSOLETE in the desktop app — it writes files as the invoking user. Keep the key only while the containerised UI still ships.

HOST_GID.description: Derived at render time from getuid()/getgid(). Not shipped and not a setting: it is a fact about the machine the app is running on, and a written-down value would pin one developer's ids into everybody's generated files.

HOST_TIMEZONE.description: Dead: no template interpolates it. Containers inherit UTC unless their image says otherwise.

ALLOWED_PHP_VERSIONS.description: Duplicates SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_PHP_VERSIONS with a DIFFERENT range (missing 5.6-7.3 and 8.5). Nothing enforces it. Delete — see C-11 and C-12.

hostPorts._note: Host-published ports for services that expose one. Only these five are parameterised; other services hardcode their port in the template or use SERVICE_<NAME>_HOST_PORT instead — an inconsistency v1 should unify.

HOST_PORT_POSTGRES.description: Older spelling of SERVICE_POSTGRES_HOST_PORT. The other six port keys are SERVICE_<ID>_HOST_PORT; these three never were, which is why the setting looked absent. Copied forward when a .env carries it, so an existing checkout keeps its ports.

HOST_PORT_PERCONA.description: There is no Percona service or template.

HOST_PORT_ADMINER.description: Dead: the Adminer template reads SERVICE_ADMINER_HOST_PORT instead. Two keys for one port, only one of them wired.

HOST_PORT_KAFKA.description: Older spelling of SERVICE_KAFKA_HOST_PORT. The other six port keys are SERVICE_<ID>_HOST_PORT; these three never were, which is why the setting looked absent. Copied forward when a .env carries it, so an existing checkout keeps its ports.

HOST_PORT_KAFKA_EXTERNAL.description: Older spelling of SERVICE_KAFKA_EXTERNAL_HOST_PORT. The other six port keys are SERVICE_<ID>_HOST_PORT; these three never were, which is why the setting looked absent. Copied forward when a .env carries it, so an existing checkout keeps its ports.

STACKVO_DRY_RUN.description: A real dry-run mode would be genuinely useful in the desktop app — implement it rather than deleting the key.

STACKVO_VERSION.description: Optional and informational: the desktop app shows it when a workspace carries one, so an existing StackVo checkout still says which version it is. A workspace the app created has no version of its own — the binary that made it is the version — so it is not written into a fresh .env and nothing falls back.

catalog._note: The capability catalog the UI renders in the new-project form (GET /api/supported-languages). This is REFERENCE DATA masquerading as configuration — it describes what StackVo can build, not what the user configured. v1 keeps the keys for compatibility but the desktop app reads catalog.json instead.

SUPPORTED_SERVERS.description: Matches the generators on disk exactly. Authoritative.

SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES.description: Advertises SIX runtimes; only php and nodejs have generators. Selecting python/go/ruby/rust in the UI produces a broken project — see C-02.

SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_PHP_VERSIONS.description: Offers 5.6-7.4, but php-extensions.sh assumes 8.0+ throughout (is_builtin_extension defaults to 8.0). See C-13.

SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_PHP_EXTENSIONS.description: The pickable extension catalog. MUST be a subset of the keys in php-extensions.json — enforced by tools/validate-contracts.mjs.

SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_PHP_EXTENSIONS_DEFAU.description: Pre-checked set in the UI. Contains 'imap', which is removed in PHP 8.2+ while the default PHP is 8.4 — the out-of-the-box selection cannot build. See C-06.

SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_NODEJS_DEFAULT.note: The env KEY says NODEJS but the stackvo.json manifest key is 'node'. See C-01.

PHP_DEFAULT_TOOLS.description: Recognised values: composer, nodejs, git, wget, unzip. Unknown values silently produce nothing.

PHP_DEFAULT_APT_PACKAGES.description: Baked into every PHP image. Includes debugging tools (strace, vim, nano, htop) — appropriate for a dev environment, but it is ~200MB of image weight worth making opt-in.

PHP_TOOL_NODEJS_VERSION.description: Node bundled INSIDE the PHP image. Differs from SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_NODEJS_DEFAULT=22 — intentional or not, it is undocumented. See C-12.

servicePattern.description: Every service is configured by a SERVICE_<NAME>_* key family. <NAME> is the service id uppercased with '-' replaced by '_' (mongo-express -> MONGO_EXPRESS).

SERVICE_<NAME>_ENABLE.description: Gates BOTH generation and the compose profile. The CLI derives `--profile <name-lowercased>` from every key matching ^SERVICE_([A-Z_]+)_ENABLE$ set to true.

SERVICE_<NAME>_VERSIONS.description: Comma-separated image tags the settings sheet offers for SERVICE_<NAME>_VERSION, newest first, with the shipped default among them. Every entry is verified against the registry the template pulls from — see examples/service_tags.rs. An offer, not a constraint: the field accepts an unlisted tag. Setting it empty removes the list and restores a plain text field.

SERVICE_<NAME>_URL.description: Traefik subdomain label; present on web-facing tools only.

SERVICE_<NAME>_HOST_PORT.description: Host-published port. Coexists inconsistently with the HOST_PORT_<NAME> family — v1 SHOULD standardise on this one.

profileDerivation.rule: SERVICE_MONGO_EXPRESS_ENABLE=true yields `--profile mongo_express`, but the compose profile in the template is `mongo-express`. Underscore vs dash: verify per service — see C-09.

services._note: The service ids a project manifest may declare. It began as the 25 directories under core/templates/services/ and was held equal to them by a test. Those directories are gone: nothing is embedded, services come from the package catalogue, and this list is now what it always read as — the vocabulary, not an inventory. It grows when the catalogue does, which is why solr, clickhouse, dragonfly, soketi, prometheus and graylog are here with no template behind them — the last four were published as packages and left out of this list, and every project declaring one was told, wrongly, that this version does not know it. An id absent from here is reported to the user as one this version does not know, so a package that is installable and unlisted would be a correct declaration met with a wrong warning.

serviceDependencies._note: core/ui/server/config/serviceDependencies.json declares only 3 entries and references a 'prometheus' service that does not exist. Six admin UIs have hard dependencies that are undeclared, so the UI happily starts them against nothing. v1 completes the graph.

grafana.note: A dashboard with no data source behind it draws nothing. Optional rather than required because a Grafana pointed at somebody else's Prometheus is a legitimate setup, and this file's own note records the opposite mistake: the version before packages referenced a prometheus that did not exist.

graylog.note: Graylog needs two stores and only one of them is a service here: its MONGODB_URI points at stackvo-mongo, while the search half ships inside the package as an OpenSearch companion and comes up with it.

phpmyadmin.note: SERVICE_PHPMYADMIN_HOST points at stackvo-mysql by default but ARBITRARY=1 allows any host.

secrets.policy: This file contains credentials (SERVICE_*_PASSWORD, *_TOKEN, *_SERVER_ID). It is gitignored and MUST stay so. The desktop app MUST redact any key matching /(PASSWORD|PASS|TOKEN|SECRET|SERVER_ID)$/ in logs, telemetry and error reports.
secrets.committedSecretWarning: SERVICE_BLACKFIRE_SERVER_ID and SERVICE_BLACKFIRE_SERVER_TOKEN carry real-looking values in .env.example. If those are live Blackfire credentials they are published in the repo and must be rotated.

_measurement.method: tools/measure-env-usage.mjs — literal grep over the checkout's core/, plus an explicit allowance for the SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES_* family, which supported-languages.js builds from a template string.
_measurement.note: The first pass of this measurement was run from the wrong working directory and reported zero consumers for every key, which made 17 keys look dead. Two of them (DEFAULT_TLD_SUFFIX, CACHE_TTL) were live, and two keys marked active (CACHE_ENABLE, LOG_ENABLE) were dead. Re-run the tool rather than trusting the labels.
